exposure: Bilateral Internal Iliac arteries ligation (BIIAL) for life-threatening obstetric hemorrhage
outcome: Future fertility (fertility positive, time to fertility)
Subsequent pregnancy outcomes (full term delivery, medical termination of pregnancy, preterm delivery, miscarriage, ectopic pregnancy)
Comorbidities in subsequent pregnancy (Gestational hypertension, Gestational Diabetes mellitus, Anaemia)
Recurrence of complications (hemorrhage, hysterectomy, uterine rupture)
Mode of delivery in subsequent pregnancy
cohort: 85 pregnant women who experienced major obstetric haemorrhage during childbirth that was controlled using Bilateral Internal Iliac arteries ligation in Chennai, India, between January 2016 and December 2020.
finding: 77.6% of women who underwent BIIAL for obstetric hemorrhage subsequently showed fertility positive results, with most achieving fertility within 1-2 years.
mod_finding: The initial delivery mode for the BIIAL procedure was predominantly LSCS (92.9%), and LSCS was also the most common mode of delivery in subsequent pregnancies (49.4%).
followup_time: At least 3-4 years for some participants, as fertility was observed within 1-2 years for 48.5% and 3-4 years for 34.8% after BIIAL surgery.
